item.title: Microsoft Job Fear Meets Oracle Cuts
item.description: The signal is no longer that AI might someday change work. The signal is that companies are already using it to redraw roles, expectations, and leverage. The human task is to stop treating identity as a job title and start naming the value that travels with you.

item.title: AI Lays Off America While Apple Launches Siri
item.description: AI is no longer the future of work — it's the present reason people are losing it. But the people who thrive will be those who treat AI as a collaborator, not a replacement. The Great Repurpose isn't a luxury anymore; it's a survival skill.

item.title: AI reshapes work, identity, and creativity
Creative Control In The Age Of AI
item.description: The old guard of creative ownership is fighting back — Adobe's Creator Act, Epidemic Sound's Creator Economy Report, and a Forbes piece on AI agents all point to the same inflection point: human creators are demanding legal and technical guardrails over their work. The Great Repurpose isn't just about adapting to AI — it's about asserting who owns the output and who gets to decide. 1. AI Agents Put Creative Control Back on the Table

item.title: Daily TGR Signal
item.description: "Creativity is really that sweet spot. People feel it will be useful in a world of automation and AI and also that it is less replaceable by these technologies."

item.title: Anthropic Files IPO, Sanders Demands Public AI Equity, Banks Cut 7K Jobs To AI
item.description: The infrastructure layer of AI is consolidating into monopoly-scale valuations (Anthropic's $965B IPO filing) while the labor layer is being dismantled in real time (7,000 Standard Chartered job cuts). The gap between capital concentration and worker displacement is widening faster than policy can respond. Sanders' sovereign wealth fund proposal is the first serious attempt to build a dam.

item.title: AI Accelerates, Humans Displace
item.description: The pattern this week is unmistakable: AI adoption is no longer about augmentation — it's about replacement at scale. Meta, Cloudflare, and others are cutting headcount precisely as their AI systems absorb human labor. The question isn't whether jobs will change; it's whether people have the inner foundation to survive the transition with their identity intact.
